conviction_note: The evidence leans slightly positive on the forward guide: two quarters running the company guided above consensus, and Q4 consensus of $266-268m implies only ~+4% QoQ. Against that sit a +9.4 put skew, a +12% 5-day run-up into the print, and a reaction history that mostly damps good prints (-0.04%, -4.89%, -1.27% on three of the last four). Neutron's 2027 slip (8-K, 2026-10-14) is public and priced. So p_up is 52, not higher, on an abs move of 9% (event-implied 8.27%, realised vol 107%, a new-period Q4 guide and a Neutron window on the call). That gives +0.36 scaled, against a findings sum of +0.5. The two agree in sign and roughly in size.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue ~$255-257m: Earnings Whispers $256.5m (https://finviz.com/news/413866/rocket-labs-q3-report-puts-neutrons-narrowing-launch-window-ahead-of-record-revenue, 2026-11-02) and Benzinga $254.5-257.0m (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/RKLB/earnings-forecasts). Both sit inside the company guide of $250-265m, with GAAP GM 29-31%, non-GAAP GM 35-37% and adj EBITDA loss $17-23m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001819994/000181999426000061/rklb-08102026ex991.htm). Q4 revenue consensus is $265.8-267.8m (Benzinga, two pages). The EPS bar is disputed (non-GAAP -$0.02 at EW against -$0.06/-$0.07 at Benzinga), so no finding rests on EPS.
positioning_check: Short interest is ~45.3m shares, 7.6% of shares outstanding, 2.0 days to cover, as of 2026-11-04 (https://equibles.com/stocks/rklb/shortinterest; aggregator, not FINRA direct; Curved Trading had 45.8m / 2.4 DTC on 2026-07-15). That is not crowded. The 25-delta skew is +9.44 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.79 and ATM IV 132%. The stock is -61% from its 52-week high of ~$151 and +48% off the low, 5-day +12.2% after the post-Neutron-delay low near $49-51. Earnings Whispers says bullish sentiment fell from 8% to 3% (2026-11-02).

findings.finding: Rocket Lab has guided the next quarter above consensus two quarters running: the Q2 guide of $225-240m was above consensus, and the Q3 guide of $250-265m had its low end above the $238.5m consensus. Q4 2026 consensus revenue is only $265.8-267.8m (Benzinga), +3-4% QoQ on a ~$257m Q3, while revenue grew +17% QoQ in Q2 and the Q3 guide midpoint implies +10%. A Q4 guide midpoint above ~$268m is the more likely outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 print (2026-08-10): next-quarter revenue guided above consensus but the GAAP GM guide (29-31%) came in below the Street's ~37.6%. Stock -0.04%. Q1 2026 print (2026-05-07): Q2 guide raised and above consensus, +34.22%. Q4 2025 print -4.89%, Q3 2025 -1.27% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected the usual above-consensus guide, Q4 consensus would sit near the trend of $275-285m and not $266-268m. Instead consensus is anchored to a cautious extrapolation after the Neutron slip, and the skew pays for downside, not upside.
findings.independence: Reuters via search summary (Q3 guide $250-265m vs $238.5m consensus) and the 2026-08-10 8-K ex99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001819994/000181999426000061/rklb-08102026ex991.htm). Q2 2026 guide above consensus: https://www.marketbeat.com/articles/rocket-lab-posts-record-q1-revenue-raises-q2-guidance/. This is a pattern inference, not a company statement about Q4.

findings.finding: Q3 bookings already disclosed at the Q2 print point to a record backlog. The 2026-08-10 release said more than $1B of contracts had been signed in Q3 to date, including options (SB-AMTI $397M, GEO >$160M, a $266M Space Force HASTE award on 2026-07-27), against a $2.36B Q2 backlog and ~$257m of Q3 revenue burn. That puts Q3 backlog at roughly $2.8-3.2B, depending on how much of the options is booked.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 record backlog of $2.36B (+137% YoY) came with a -0.04% reaction. Backlog headlines have not by themselves moved this stock on recent prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The individual awards are public. A '$3B backlog' headline is arithmetic the market can do, so it is mostly priced. The residual is the share of options booked as backlog, which no preview quantifies (previews still quote $2.36B).
findings.independence: $266M HASTE award release, 2026-07-27: https://rocketlabcorp.com/updates/record-contract-rslp-kodiak/ (one of the >$1B Q3 contracts, so not fully independent).

findings.finding: Electron flew 5 times in Q3 2026: launches 14-18 of the year, the 97th Electron on 2026-09-26. Q2 had 7 (the 13th of the year on 2026-06-30) and Q1 had 6 (10-Q). Launch Services revenue ($44.6m in Q2, 19% of revenue) is therefore likely flat to down QoQ. Space Systems ($189.5m in Q2, 81%) has to carry the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print in the baseline turned on launch count. Q2 2026 launch revenue fell YoY ($44.6m vs $46.6m) inside a 62% total beat, and the stock was -0.04%.
findings.why_not_priced: Launch counts are public, but the Q3 guide was set on 2026-08-10 with the manifest known, so this lands inside guidance. Net of Space Systems growth (81% of revenue, +94% YoY in Q2), the revenue effect is near zero.
findings.independence: 96th Electron / 17th of 2026 release, 2026-09-19 (https://investors.rocketlabcorp.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mission-success-rocket-lab-launches-96th-electron-mission). The 13th of 2026 on 2026-06-30 is from the Stocktwits launch preview (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/rklb-worst-month-ever-13th-electron-launch-bulls-fresh-fuel/cZ1BMuvR7Wz). Q1 = 6 launches from the Q1 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001819994/000181999426000028/rklb-20260331.htm). Q4 cadence on track: the 98th Electron / 19th of 2026 flew on 2026-10-21 (https://rocketlabcorp.com/updates/mission-success-rocket-lab-launches-98th-electron-mission/).

findings.finding: The Q2 margin and EBITDA beat was flattered by one-offs that do not repeat in Q3. The Q2 10-Q shows an $8.1m net favourable cumulative catch-up on contract estimates ($5.9m on one contract), and a call summary cites a non-recurring tariff refund. The same 10-Q discloses projected late deliveries on the MDA (Globalstar bus) contract with liquidated damages possible and the net amount undeterminable. Q3 GAAP GM is already guided down to 29-31% from 36.1%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 GAAP GM guide below the Street (29-31% vs ~37.6%) coincided with a flat reaction (-0.04%) despite a big adj EBITDA beat (-$8.8m vs a guide of -$20m to -$26m).
findings.why_not_priced: The GM step-down is guided and so mostly priced. The MDA liquidated-damages exposure sits in a 10-Q revenue note no preview mentions. If it were priced, previews would flag a possible charge or EAC reversal on the Globalstar buses.
findings.independence: Q2 call summary on the tariff refund and Neutron Flight 2 inventory reserve: https://www.stocktaper.com/earningsCallSummary/RKLB/2026/Q2. The GM guide below the Street: https://parameter.io/rocket-lab-rklb-stock-plunges-9-on-weak-q3-margin-forecast/ (date unverified; may be the Q3 2025 print). Shares the 10-Q with the backlog and ATM findings only as a document, not as a fact.

findings.finding: Neutron's first launch slipped from Q4 2026 to 2027 (8-K, 2026-10-14) after voids were found in a forward tank dome, and the stock fell ~11% that day. The company set no new timeframe, and press reports put first-stage tank assembly and testing into Q1 2027. The call will be the first chance to give a 2027 window. Every Neutron update since 2025 has been a slip.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Neutron delay announcements: 2026-10-14 about -11% (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/15/rocket-lab-tumbles-11-as-neutrons-first-flight-moves-to-2027-spacex-and-ast-spacemobile-pull-back/). Feb 2026 slip to late 2026 about -9.5% (https://trendspider.com/blog/rklb-stock-slides-9-after-neutron-launch-delay-to-late-2026/). Nov 2025 slip to 2026 at the Q3 2025 print, -1.27% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The 2027 slip itself is priced: the stock fell to ~$50. What is not priced is the window. A 'H1 2027' would read as relief and 'H2 2027' or no date as another slip, and nothing public settles which. The sign is close to a coin toss, with a slight lean negative on this programme's record.
findings.independence: Space.com 2026-10-14 (https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/rocket-lab-pushes-1st-launch-of-next-gen-neutron-rocket-to-2027) and Via Satellite 2026-10-15 (https://www.satellitetoday.com/launch/2026/10/15/rocket-labs-neutron-debut-now-delayed-to-2027/). Same event, not independent of the 8-K.

findings.finding: Rocket Lab replaced its ATM on 2026-08-13 with a $1.94B program (Deutsche Bank and Wells Fargo agents, forward sales allowed) to fund the $27/share cash leg of the ~$8.0B Iridium deal and cut the $3.6B bridge loan. In Q2 it sold 8.15m ATM shares for $1.07B net (~$131/share). The Q3 10-Q will show how much it sold as the stock fell from ~$150 toward ~$60, and the post-print end of blackout reopens ATM supply inside the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A $1B ATM overhang was blamed for weakness ahead of the Q1 2026 print (https://rallies.ai/news/rocket-lab-slides-as-1b-atm-equity-program-overhangs-shares-ahead-of-q1-report), which then reacted +34.2%. No print reaction tied to ATM disclosure.
findings.why_not_priced: The program is public. What the market has not seen is how much was sold in Q3 and at what prices, which only the Q3 10-Q discloses. Previews quote liquidity of ~$2.4B as of June. The money buys a visible acquisition (Iridium: $872m revenue, 57% OEBITDA margin), not distress, so the only negative is supply.
findings.independence: Q2 10-Q ATM proceeds of $1.53B for the half (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001819994/000181999426000062/rklb-20260630.htm). Iridium deal 8-K with the $3.6B bridge (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001819994/000175392626001085/g085783_ex99-1.htm).

outside_window.finding: Globalstar asked the FCC (filings of 2026-11-02, reported 11-03/11-04) to scrutinise the Rocket Lab-Iridium deal over Rocket Lab's role as Globalstar's bus supplier via MDA. SpaceX and Ligado also raised concerns. The FCC licence transfer is still pending; HSR cleared in August 2026 and Iridium holders approved on 2026-09-24. An FCC decision falls long after the window.
Neutron first flight in 2027. Success or failure of first-stage tank qualification (Q1 2027 per press) and the inaugural launch are the real catalysts.

baseline_tension: The small positive lean, a Q4 guide likely above a low consensus, cuts against the +9.4 put skew, and part of the low-expectations case was used up by the +12% 5-day run-up. The positive findings are therefore kept small and p_up held at 52.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name damps good prints: -0.04, -4.89, -1.27) and rule 7 (a positive sign against a +9.4 put skew): Q4 guide finding cut from +1.5 to +1.0, p_up from 53 to 52.
Rule 7: positioning finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2 because the 5-day +12% run-up has used up part of the washed-out-sentiment cushion.

Rule 4 (financing is a question): the ATM funds a visible acquisition (Iridium cash leg), not distress, so the financing finding was cut from -0.5 to -0.3 and kept negative only for supply returning after the blackout.
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): Electron launch-count finding cut from -0.3 to -0.1, because Launch is 19% of revenue and Space Systems (81%, +94% YoY) carries the guide.

Rule 6 (inside what was guided): the GM/one-off finding cut from -0.5 to -0.3 because the GM step-down is inside the guided range; backlog cut from +0.5 to +0.4 because the contracts were pre-disclosed. The EPS bar is disputed, so no finding rests on it and the revenue bar (two agreeing sources plus guide) is used.
Neutron (-0.3), insider sales (-0.1) and Iridium Q3 (0.0) left standing.
